extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or graduate students studying functional analysis/operator theory
extracted.subtask_description: Worked solutions and statements of standard results in Hilbert/Banach space operator theory (compact operators, spectra, projections, Lax–Milgram applications, Ascoli–Arzelà compactness, etc.), intended to accompany textbook exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left inverse existence criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is injective and R(T) (the range of T) is closed (in a Hilbert space), then T has a left inverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used/deduced from Theorem 2.13; the fact that R(T) has a complement in a Hilbert space is invoked to conclude existence of a left inverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of N(S) via variational inequality / orthogonality
rubrics_metrics.description: u ∈ N(S) iff (Sv, v − u) ≥ 0 for all v ∈ H; equivalently u ∈ R(S)⊥ implies (Sv − Su, v) ≥ 0 ∀v and leads to (Su, v) = 0 ∀v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace v by tv to deduce linear relations; shows equivalence between nullspace membership and orthogonality/variational inequalities (see also related exercises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Lax–Milgram for coercive bilinear forms
rubrics_metrics.description: When the bilinear form is continuous and coercive, existence and uniqueness of solutions follow by the Lax–Milgram theorem (Corollary 5.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used several times to obtain weak/strong solutions and invertibility of associated operators (e.g., establishing bijectivity of second-order operators or positivity-based bijectivity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolvent-type approximation by (I + tS)^{-1}
rubrics_metrics.description: For ut = (I + tS)^{-1} f one has different asymptotic behavior depending on decomposition of f: if f ∈ N(S) then ut = f for all t; if f ∈ R(S) then ut → 0 as t → ∞; in general ut → PN(S)f weakly and even strongly under additional inequalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two methods shown: (a) direct estimate |ut| ≤ (1/t)|v| for f = Sv and density argument; (b) energy/weak-compactness argument passing to subsequences, showing Su = 0 and eventual strong convergence using (Sut,ut) ≥ 0 and limsup bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection onto closed convex set: convergence and uniqueness of weak limits
rubrics_metrics.description: For sequence (un) in H with projection PK onto closed convex K, (PK un) is Cauchy under given inequalities; any weak limit of (un) is the projection of the weak limit; uniqueness of limit implies weak convergence of whole sequence to the projection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses monotonicity (un − PK un, v − PK un) ≤ 0 ∀v ∈ K, passage to limits along subsequences, Riesz representation to identify limits, and standard projection properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascoli–Arzelà criterion for compactness of operator images
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator T maps the unit ball into an equicontinuous, uniformly bounded family of functions on a compact set, then T(B_E) has compact closure in C([0,1]) (hence compact in Lp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to show compactness of certain integral or smoothing operators (e.g., operators with modulus of continuity bound |Tu(x) − Tu(y)| ≤ C|x − y|^{α}||u||_p) and reference to Ascoli–Arzelà theorem for BF compactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak-to-strong continuity leads to finite-dimensional range
rubrics_metrics.description: If a linear operator T is continuous from E endowed with weak topology into F with strong topology, then R(T) is finite-dimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a neighborhood basis in the weak topology defined by finitely many linear functionals, constructs a finite-codimension subspace M on which T vanishes, and concludes R(T)=T(N) is finite-dimensional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fredholm-type inequality criterion (closed range + finite-dimensional kernel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of a projection P onto N(T) and constant C with ||u||_E ≤ C(||T u||_F + ||P u||_E) for all u implies T has closed range and finite-dimensional nullspace (and conversely certain compactness/sequence arguments yield the inequality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to prove equivalence between several formulations (A),(B),(C) in Exercise 6.9: introduce complement E0, use open mapping theorem for T|E0, and use compactness of certain Q(un) sequences in necessity directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perturbation/invertibility and distance to spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: If (T − λI)^{-1} exists and ||(T − λI)^{-1}|| is finite, then dist(λ, σ(T)) ≥ 1/||(T − λI)^{-1}||; small norm of resolvent gives spectral distance lower bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: if μ satisfies |μ − λ|·||(T − λI)^{-1}|| < 1 then μ ∈ ρ(T); hence the stated lower bound on distance to spectrum (Proposition applied in Exercise 6.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial spectral mapping and point-spectrum relations
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q is a real polynomial and μ ∈ Q(σ(T)) then μ ∈ σ(Q(T)); more precisely, EV(Q(T)) ⊂ Q(EV(T)) (and converses follow under injectivity/real-root factoring), with constraints on real roots used in arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use factorization Q(t) − μ = (t − t1)...(t − tq)·Q1(t) and injectivity of (T − ti I) factors when ti ∉ EV(T) to deduce contradictions if eigenvectors existed outside Q(EV(T)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact self-adjoint operator spectral structure (existence of eigenpairs accumulating at 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a compact self-adjoint operator T there exists a sequence of eigenpairs (μ_n, u_n) with μ_n > 0, μ_n → 0 and ||u_n|| = 1, satisfying T u_n = μ_n u_n (i.e., discrete spectrum with possible accumulation at 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in discussion of compact, self-adjoint operators (Section 8.x): use compactness and spectral theorems to get orthonormal eigenfunctions and eigenvalues tending to 0; used to link operator equation to ODE eigenvalue problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for surjectivity/injectivity via closedness and complements
rubrics_metrics.description: If E0 is a complement of N(T) and T|E0 is bijective onto R(T), the open mapping theorem yields a norm inequality ||u||_E ≤ C||T u||_F for u ∈ E0; conversely, compactness-type estimates on projections and images lead to surjectivity/closed-range conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used repeatedly (e.g., Exercise 6.9, 6.8) to move between algebraic decompositions (complements, projections) and analytic norm inequalities, combining with open mapping and compactness arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of energy/monotonicity inequalities to upgrade weak limits to strong limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Given sequences ut with bounds ||ut|| ≤ ||f|| and inequalities like (Sut, ut) ≥ 0 and limsup_t ||ut||^2 ≤ (f,u) = ||u||^2, one can deduce strong convergence ut → u from weak convergence plus energy inequalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in the resolvent-type method (Exercise 5.20): pass to subsequences, identify weak limit in N(S), use orthogonality properties and limsup estimates to conclude strong convergence of the whole family.
